Lay the glasses diagonally on the surface with both temples fully opened backward, clearly separated and extending in the same direction without crossing or forming an X. Photograph from a high three-quarter overhead angle rather than a straight top view, placing the front frame near the lower right while the temples lead toward the upper left. Use a continuous pale blue paper surface with a darker blue background and one restrained diagonal tonal transition. Soft directional light creates a long but controlled shadow while keeping the frame edges precise. Treat both lenses as clear_optical: keep them highly transparent, clean, and nearly colorless, with the background continuing naturally through them at the same tone, brightness, saturation, and texture. Allow only faint physically plausible surface or edge reflections; no gray haze, milky white, frosting, glow, uniform blue tint, mirror finish, or empty plastic-hole appearance. Any blue cast must come from the shared scene lighting and affect the frame and paper as well, never as a uniform lens tint. Single product, no extra accessories, no added text or watermark.
